questions.question: What is the nature of the key intermediate formed when methylmagnesium bromide adds to acetone?

options.label: A
options.text: A tetrahedral magnesium alkoxide intermediate [(CH₃)₃C-O⁻ MgBr⁺] resulting from nucleophilic attack of the carbanionic methyl group on the carbonyl carbon.

options.label: B
options.text: A cyclic 4-membered oxetane ring.

options.label: C
options.text: A radical pair involving acetyl radical.

options.label: D
options.text: A planar secondary carbocation.

questions.correct_answer: A tetrahedral magnesium alkoxide intermediate [(CH₃)₃C-O⁻ MgBr⁺] resulting from nucleophilic attack of the carbanionic methyl group on the carbonyl carbon.
questions.explanation: Nucleophilic addition of the polarized organomagnesium carbanion into the carbonyl π* orbital produces a tetrahedral magnesium alkoxide.

questions.topic: Incompatibility of Grignard with Protic Groups
questions.question: Why does phenylmagnesium bromide immediately fail if water, alcohols, or amines are present?

options.label: A
options.text: Water oxidizes the magnesium to magnesium peroxide.

options.label: B
options.text: Protic solvents dissolve the organic substrate permanently.

options.label: C
options.text: The Grignard reagent acts as a powerful Brønsted base (pKa of benzene ~ 43), undergoing instant irreversible protonation to benzene and basic Mg salts.

options.label: D
options.text: Amines polymerize the Grignard reagent.

questions.correct_answer: The Grignard reagent acts as a powerful Brønsted base (pKa of benzene ~ 43), undergoing instant irreversible protonation to benzene and basic Mg salts.
questions.explanation: Grignard reagents are superbases and are instantly destroyed by protic hydrogens (water, alcohols, carboxylic acids, amines).

questions.question: Why does pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) in anhydrous CH₂Cl₂ stop at the aldehyde stage when oxidizing 1-hexanol?

options.label: A
options.text: PCC lacks the oxidation potential to oxidize aldehydes.

options.label: B
options.text: Because the absence of water prevents hydration of the aldehyde to a gem-diol (aldehyde hydrate), which is required for the second chromate oxidation to carboxylic acid.

options.label: C
options.text: PCC only oxidizes tertiary alcohols.

options.label: D
options.text: PCC precipitates as an insoluble chromium metal.

questions.correct_answer: Because the absence of water prevents hydration of the aldehyde to a gem-diol (aldehyde hydrate), which is required for the second chromate oxidation to carboxylic acid.
questions.explanation: Jones reagent in aqueous acid forms the gem-diol hydrate, which undergoes a second oxidation; anhydrous PCC avoids hydrate formation.

questions.question: In the Swern oxidation of secondary alcohols, what reactive electrophile activates DMSO?

options.label: A
options.text: Peracetic acid zwitterion.

options.label: B
options.text: Chromium trioxide pyridine complex.

options.label: C
options.text: Diazomethane gas.

options.label: D
options.text: Dimethylchlorosulfonium cation [Me₂S⁺-Cl], formed by reaction of DMSO with oxalyl chloride, releasing CO₂, CO, and chloride.

questions.correct_answer: Dimethylchlorosulfonium cation [Me₂S⁺-Cl], formed by reaction of DMSO with oxalyl chloride, releasing CO₂, CO, and chloride.
questions.explanation: Oxalyl chloride activates DMSO to generate the electrophilic dimethylchlorosulfonium species, which coordinates alcohol oxygen.

questions.question: What reactive intermediate is generated when (R)-2-butanol reacts with phosphorus tribromide (PBr₃)?

options.label: A
options.text: A protonated alkyl dibromophosphite intermediate [R-O⁺(H)-PBr₂], which is displaced by bromide in a clean SN2 backside attack with inversion.

options.label: B
options.text: A cyclic phosphorus ylide.

options.label: C
options.text: A free alkyl radical intermediate.

options.label: D
options.text: A planar secondary carbocation with complete racemization.

questions.correct_answer: A protonated alkyl dibromophosphite intermediate [R-O⁺(H)-PBr₂], which is displaced by bromide in a clean SN2 backside attack with inversion.
questions.explanation: PBr₃ converts the poor -OH leaving group into an excellent phosphite leaving group, which bromide displaces via SN2 with inversion.

questions.question: Why does the reaction of (R)-2-octanol with SOCl₂ in the presence of pyridine proceed with inversion of configuration?

options.label: A
options.text: The chlorosulfite intermediate undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift.

options.label: B
options.text: The reaction proceeds via an internal SNi frontside attack.

options.label: C
options.text: Pyridine captures HCl to form pyridinium chloride; free chloride ion then carries out an SN2 backside displacement on the alkyl chlorosulfite intermediate.

options.label: D
options.text: Pyridine acts as a radical initiator that flips the bond.

questions.correct_answer: Pyridine captures HCl to form pyridinium chloride; free chloride ion then carries out an SN2 backside displacement on the alkyl chlorosulfite intermediate.
questions.explanation: In the presence of pyridine, chloride ion is liberated to perform an intermolecular SN2 attack, inverting stereochemistry.

questions.question: Why does tosylation of (S)-2-butanol with TsCl and pyridine yield (S)-2-butyl tosylate with 100% retention of configuration?

options.label: A
options.text: Because pyridine forces double inversion at carbon.

options.label: B
options.text: Because TsCl is a chiral reagent.

options.label: C
options.text: Because the reaction occurs at the oxygen atom (O-S bond formation), leaving the chiral C-O carbon stereocenter completely untouched.

options.label: D
options.text: Because tosylate forms a planar carbocation that reforms the S-enantiomer.

questions.correct_answer: Because the reaction occurs at the oxygen atom (O-S bond formation), leaving the chiral C-O carbon stereocenter completely untouched.
questions.explanation: Tosylation forms an O-S bond without breaking the chiral C-O bond, preserving the absolute configuration of the carbon.

questions.question: What is the driving force and mechanistic sequence in the pinacol rearrangement of 2,3-dimethylbutane-2,3-diol?

options.label: A
options.text: Loss of two water molecules to form a conjugated diene.

options.label: B
options.text: Homolytic cleavage to form two acetone molecules.

options.label: C
options.text: Protonation and loss of water yields a 3° carbocation, followed by a 1,2-methyl shift driven by lone-pair resonance stabilization from the adjacent hydroxyl oxygen to form pinacolone.

options.label: D
options.text: Deprotonation to form a stable epoxide.

questions.correct_answer: Protonation and loss of water yields a 3° carbocation, followed by a 1,2-methyl shift driven by lone-pair resonance stabilization from the adjacent hydroxyl oxygen to form pinacolone.
questions.explanation: The 1,2-alkyl shift transforms a tertiary carbocation into an exceptionally stable resonance-stabilized oxocarbenium ion.

questions.topic: Periodic Acid Cleavage of Vicinal Diols
questions.question: What is the key cyclic intermediate during the oxidative cleavage of cis-cyclohexane-1,2-diol by periodic acid (HIO₄)?

options.label: A
options.text: A cyclic five-membered periodate diester intermediate that undergoes concerted two-electron fragmentation to yield a dialdehyde and iodic acid.

options.label: B
options.text: A six-membered ozonide ring.

options.label: C
options.text: A diradical iodate intermediate.

options.label: D
options.text: A bridged oxonium cation.

questions.correct_answer: A cyclic five-membered periodate diester intermediate that undergoes concerted two-electron fragmentation to yield a dialdehyde and iodic acid.
questions.explanation: Vicinal diols condense with periodic acid to form a cyclic periodate ester, which fragments via a concerted pericyclic pathway.

questions.question: Why does phenol completely resist acid-catalyzed dehydration compared to cyclohexanol?

options.label: A
options.text: Phenol is a stronger base than sulfuric acid.

options.label: B
options.text: Phenol has no lone pairs on oxygen.

options.label: C
options.text: Phenol undergoes spontaneous combustion in acid.

options.label: D
options.text: Loss of water would require forming an extremely unstable, high-energy phenyl cation (sp-hybridized vacant orbital) and destroying aromaticity.

questions.correct_answer: Loss of water would require forming an extremely unstable, high-energy phenyl cation (sp-hybridized vacant orbital) and destroying aromaticity.
questions.explanation: Aromatic rings cannot support carbocations in the sp² plane, making dehydration to benzyne thermodynamically prohibitive in acid.
